title: Periodic Table and Properties - Chemistry - Chemical Significance
subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Based on periodic trends, which Alkali Metal is expected to react most violently with water?
questions.explain: Reactivity of alkali metals increases down the group because ionization energy decreases. Cesium loses its electron most easily, leading to the fastest and most explosive reaction with water.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Conversely, for Halogens (Group 17), reactivity decreases down the group. Why is Fluorine more reactive than Iodine?
options: Fluorine has a lower electron affinity
Fluorine has a much higher electronegativity and stronger oxidizing power
Fluorine has a larger atomic radius
Iodine is a gas while Fluorine is solid
questions.explain: Halogens react by gaining electrons. Fluorine has the strongest tendency to attract electrons (electronegativity) and oxidize other substances. As size increases (down the group), this attraction weakens.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Metallic character refers to the tendency to lose electrons. How does this trend behave in the periodic table?
options: Increases across a period, Increases down a group
Decreases across a period, Increases down a group
Increases across a period, Decreases down a group
Decreases across a period, Decreases down a group
questions.explain: Metallic character relies on low ionization energy. IE increases across a period (less metallic) and decreases down a group (more metallic). Thus, the most metallic elements are at the bottom-left.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: The nature of oxides changes across Period 3. Which of the following correctly pairs the element with the acid-base nature of its oxide?
questions.explain: Oxides trend from Basic (left) to Acidic (right). $Na_2O$ and $MgO$ are basic. $Al_2O_3$ is **amphoteric** (reacts with both acids and bases). $SO_3$ and $Cl_2O_7$ are acidic.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Which of the following is the strongest reducing agent in aqueous solution?
questions.explain: While IE decreases down the group, standard reduction potential ($E^\circ$) depends on sublimation, ionization, and hydration energy. Lithium has a very high **hydration energy** due to its small size, making it the strongest reducing agent in aqueous solution despite having a higher IE than Cs.
